Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
19-year-old female with 6-day history of dysuria, urinary frequency, and suprapubic ache; likely uncomplicated lower urinary tract infection.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Burning/stinging on micturition, increased urinary frequency for “just under a week.”  
• Associated symptoms: Pink-tinged urine noted today; mild suprapubic aching, worse during voiding.  
• Pertinent negatives: No back/flank pain, no fever, no nausea/vomiting, no abnormal vaginal discharge, bowels unchanged from baseline IBS pattern.  
• Past medical history: Irritable bowel syndrome.  
• Allergies: Clindamycin – adverse reaction (details not specified).  
• Medications: 
  – Combined oral contraceptive pill (type/dose/route/frequency not documented).  
  – Mebeverine (dose/route/frequency not documented) for IBS.  
• Social / preventive: University student living in halls; sexually active with long-term partner, no condom use, last intercourse 1–2 weeks ago; tried cannabis once; drinks alcohol socially; non-smoker.

Examination:
• Vitals: not recorded.  
• Physical exam: not performed (teleconsult).

Impression:
Uncomplicated cystitis / urinary tract infection; microscopic hematuria suspected.

Plan:
• Provide sterile urine sample today for dipstick, microscopy, culture & sensitivities.  
• Empiric oral antibiotic: Nitrofurantoin (3-day course) or Trimethoprim – final choice pending culture (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• Hydration advice: increase oral fluids.  
• Analgesia: Paracetamol as needed.  
• Safety-net: seek urgent review if develops fever, flank/back pain, or vomiting.  
• Follow-up: contact clinic if no improvement within one week or when culture results available.

Quality checks:
● Missing elements: vitals, physical exam, comprehensive medication list (doses), immunization status, pregnancy test not performed, detailed allergy reaction.  
● Internal conflicts: symptom duration initially stated “few days/three days,” later clarified to “just under a week” – conflict noted but resolved to ~6 days.  
● Transcript quality: clear; minor conversational filler, no significant inaudible sections.
